([[Mebane, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] (2004–2007) | draft_year = 2007 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 51 | draft_team = [[Chicago Bulls]] | career_start = 2007 | career_end = 2014 | career_number = 44 | career_position = [[Point guard]] | years1 = 2007–2008 | team1 = [[Iowa Energy]] | years2 = 2008 | team2 = [[Pau-Orthez]] | years3 = 2009 | team3 = Iowa Energy | years4 = 2009 | team4 = [[AEL Limassol B.C.]] | years5 = 2009–2010 | team5 = [[Springfield Armor]] | years6 = {{nbay|2009|end}} | team6 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years7 = 2010–2011 | team7 = Springfield Armor | years8 = 2011 | team8 = [[Toros de Aragua]] | years9 = 2011–2012 | team9 = Springfield Armor | years10 = 2012 | team10 = [[Basket Barcellona]] | years11 = 2013–2014 | team11 = Springfield Armor | years12 = 2014 | team12 = [[Bakersfield Jam]] | highlights = * [[NBA D-League]] All-Star (2012) * Third-team All-[[Big 12]] (2007) | bbr = curryja01 }} '''JamesOn Curry''' (born January 7, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played for [[Oklahoma State University]] from 2004 to 2007, and after forgoing his senior season, left for the [[2007 NBA draft]]. He was selected in the second round as the 51st overall pick by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. After stints in the [[NBA Development League]] and Europe, Curry made his NBA debut in January 2010, playing 3.9 seconds for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. It was Curry's only NBA regular-season appearance and set a record for the shortest NBA career of all time per in-game time spent on the court. ==Early life== Curry was born in [[Pleasant Grove, North Carolina]] to father Leon and mother Connie (née Parker) Curry.{{Cite web|url=https://okstate.com/news/2006/10/11/JamesOn_Curry.aspx|title=JamesOn Curry|website=okstate.com|access-date=April 10, 2020}} He attended [[Eastern Alamance High School]], in [[Mebane, North Carolina]]; in his freshman season, Curry scored a total of 639 points, which at the time was the highest mark for a freshman in North Carolina high school history: the record was then beaten by [[Junior Robinson (basketball)|Junior Robinson]] in 2011.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nchsaa.org/sites/default/files/attachments/Basketball-Men_0.pdf|title=MEN'S BASKETBALL|website=nchsaa.org|page=3|access-date=April 10, 2020|archive-date=August 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809205658/http://www.nchsaa.org/sites/default/files/attachments/Basketball-Men_0.pdf|url-status=dead}} In 2001, Curry scored 59 points in a game against [[Chatham High School (Virginia)|Chatham High School]] of [[Chatham, Virginia]].''MEN'S BASKETBALL'', nchsaa.org, p. 9. Curry established another single-season scoring record the following year, scoring a total of 892 points, beating the old sophomore record established by [[Scooter Sherrill]] in 1998. In his junior year, Curry scored 972 points, another North Carolina record, beating the mark of 954 that Lawrence Clayton had established in 1958. He averaged 40.2 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game as a senior and was a two-time Associated Press All-State first team selection. On December 9, 2003, Curry scored 47 points and added 9 rebounds, 9 assists and 9 steals, thus recording a near-[[quadruple-double]]. On January 19, 2004, Curry scored 65 points against [[Western Alamance High School]], two shy of the all-time North Carolina record of 67 established in 1950 by Bob Poole. During that game he shot 25 of 39 from the field (9 of 16 on three-pointers), and also recorded 11 rebounds. Curry set the all-time North Carolina high school scoring record with 3,307 points,''MEN'S BASKETBALL'', nchsaa.org, p. 8. which was surpassed in 2018 by UNC recruit [[Coby White]] with 3,573 points.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/white-coby.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109234735/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/white-coby.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 9, 2018|title=Coby White|website=usab.com|access-date=April 10, 2020}} In his high school Curry had 74 games where he scored at least 20 points (28 of them in his junior year), 44 30-plus-point games, and 16 games with 40 points or more. ==College career== Curry initially signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], but his scholarship was rescinded following pleading guilty to drug charges, and he signed with Oklahoma State University (OSU).{{cite news |last=Anderson |first=Kelli |date=February 28, 2005 |title=A jolt from JameSon |url=https://vault.si.com/vault/2005/02/28/a-jolt-from-jameson |access-date=March 21, 2022 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} As a freshman in 2004–05, Curry started 15 of 33 games played and averaged 9.4 points and 2.8 assists per game. He finished the season ranked ninth among [[Big 12]] leaders in conference games for three-point field goals made (1.75 per game). He scored 22 points on 8-for-11 shooting, in his first start versus [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] on January 30, 2005. He made six three-pointers out of 8 attempts, including 5-for-5 in the second half, in which he scored 17 of his 22.{{Cite 22, 2017|title=Oklahoma State vs. Baylor – Game Recap – March 3, 2007 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} ==Professional career== Curry was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 51st overall pick of the [[2007 NBA draft]]. On August 2, 2007, he signed with the Bulls.{{cite news| url = http://newsok.com/article/3097821 | title = Bulls sign former OSU star Curry | agency=[[Associated Press]] | date = August 2, 2007 | access-date = 2007-08-04 }}{{cite news| url = http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_signed_070802.html | title = Bulls sign JamesOn Curry | date = August 2, 2007 | work = NBA.com | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070807223532/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_signed_070802.html | archive-date = August 7, 2007}} He was assigned to their [[NBA Development League]] affiliate [[Iowa Energy]] on November 15, 2007,{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/history/alltime_transactions.html|title=Chicago Bulls All-Time Transactions|website=Chicago Bulls}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/curry_071115.html|title=Bulls Assign JamesOn Curry To Iowa Energy|website=[[NBA.com]] }} recalled on December 17,[http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/curry_071217.html Bulls Recall JamesOn Curry From Iowa Energy] reassigned to Iowa on January 7, 2008,{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/curry_080107.html|title=Bulls Re-Assign JamesOn Curry To Iowa Energy|website=[[NBA.com]] }} and recalled again on January 24.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/curry_080124.html|title=Bulls Recall Curry From Energy|website=[[NBA.com]] }} He later underwent thumb surgery.{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.chicagosports.chicagotribune.com/fullcourtpress/jameson_curry/index.html |title=Bulls waive Curry |access-date=2008-12-09 |archive-date=2009-01-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090101015254/http://blogs.chicagosports.chicagotribune.com/fullcourtpress/jameson_curry/index.html |url-status=dead }} Curry played 13 games as a starter for Iowa during the 2007–08 season, averaging 20.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 5.6 assists, 1.08 steals and 39.7 minutes per game. He also shot .463 from the floor, including .377 from three-point range, and .719 from the free throw line. He was waived by the Bulls on July 31, 2008. He did not make his debut for Chicago.{{cite news| url = http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_waived_080731.html | title = Bulls waive JamesOn Curry | work = NBA.com | date = July 31, 2008 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080805041613/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_waived_080731.html | archive-date = August 5, 2008}}{{Cite web|url=https://oklahoman.com/article/3277397/chicago-bulls-waive-guard-jameson-curry/|title=Chicago Bulls waive guard JamesOn Curry|date=July 31, 2008|website=Oklahoman.com|access-date=August 28, 2019|archive-date=August 28, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190828204143/http://oklahoman.com/article/3277397/chicago-bulls-waive-guard-jameson-curry|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3513487|title=Bulls waive '07 second-round draft pick Curry|date=July 31, 2008|website=ESPN.com}} By releasing him, the Bulls were only obligated to pay $100,000 of his partially guaranteed salary for [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]]. In August 2008, Curry signed with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|Pau-Orthez]] of the [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball|French league]],{{Cite web|url=https://thehoop.blogspot.com/2008/08/pau-orthez-signed-jameson-curry.html|title=The Hoop: Pau Orthez signed Jameson Curry|date=August 21, 2008}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.sport.fr/Basket/bas/Pro-A-Pau-Orthez-enrole-JamesOn-Curry-133979.shtm|title=Pau-Orthez enrôle JamesOn Curry|access-date=2008-12-10|archive-date=2008-09-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080903041628/http://www.sport.fr/basket/bas/Pro-A-Pau-Orthez-enrole-JamesOn-Curry-133979.shtm|url-status=dead}} but was waived in October after failing to impress the coaching staff.{{Cite web|url=https://thehoop.blogspot.com/2008/10/pau-orthez-to-replace-curry.html|title=The Hoop: Pau Orthez to replace Curry|date=October 9, 2008}} In March 2009, he re-joined the Iowa Energy for the rest of the 2008–09 D-League season.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/JamesOn-Curry/Summary/12|title=JamesOn Curry|work=RealGM.com|access-date=May 22, 2024}} Curry started the 2009–10 season with [[Proteas EKA AEL]], a Cypriot team in [[Limassol]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/jameson_curry.pdf |title=JamesOn Curry D-League profile |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2010-01-23 |archive-date=2010-01-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100120022039/http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/jameson_curry.pdf |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |date=2010-01-22 |title=Clippers Sign JamesOn Curry to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews100122b.html |access-date=2023-09-21 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} He was later selected 14th overall in the [[2009 NBA Development League draft|2009 NBA D-League Draft]] by the expansion [[Springfield Armor]]. It was their first-ever pick.{{Cite web|url=https://www.masslive.com/sports/2009/11/springfield_armor_select_forme.html|title=Springfield Armor select former Chicago Bulls guard JamesOn Curry with their first pick|first=Kyle|last=Belanger|date=November 6, 2009|website=masslive.com}} He joined the Armor for the 2009–10 season. On January 22, 2010, Curry signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] after averaging 16.1 points, 7.5 assists and 4.0 rebounds with Springfield.{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2010 |title=Clippers' Telfair out 4-6 weeks; Curry signs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4851112 |website=ESPN.com}} He was subbed into a game on January 25, playing just 3.9 seconds. This was the only time Curry would ever play in an NBA game,{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/armor-re-acquire-jameson-curry/n-3957172|title=Armor Re-Acquire JamesOn Curry|date=January 28, 2010|website=OurSports Central}} and is the shortest NBA career in terms of time played.{{Cite web |last=Bois |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Bois |date=December 30, 2019 |title=The 10 least consequential athletes of the decade |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2019/12/30/21035159/the-10-least-consequential-athletes-of-the-decade |access-date=January 1, 2020 |website=SBNation}}{{Cite web |last=Bassett |first=Bailey |date=2023-11-28 |title=10 players who played fewest minutes in NBA history |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/nba-stories/10-players-who-played-fewest-minutes-nba-history |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=ClutchPoints |language=en}} He was released by the Clippers on January 26, when the team acquired [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2010-jan-27-la-sp-clippers-fyi27-2010jan27-story.html|title=Clippers acquire guard Bobby Brown from New Orleans|date=January 27, 2010|website=Los Angeles Times}} He returned to the Armor, where he was later waived on March 3, 2010, due to injury. Curry re-joined the Springfield Armor for the 2010–11 season. Following the D-League season, he had a stint in Venezuela with [[Toros de Aragua]] during the 2011 [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto|LBP]] season.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Jameson-Curry/71937|title=JamesOn Curry|work=usbasket.com|access-date=May 22, 2024|url-access=subscription}} Curry returned to the Armor for the 2011–12 season and was selected to play in the 2012 NBA D-League All-Star Game. In May 2012, he joined [[Basket Barcellona]] in Italy. On November 1, 2013, Curry was re-acquired by the Springfield Armor.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005917/http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/returning_players_for_2013201_2013_11_01.html|url-status=dead|title=Returning Players Highlight Initial Training Camp Invites|website=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=December 4, 2013}} On January 2, 2014, he was traded to the [[Bakersfield Jam]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jam_trade_for_jameson_curry_2014_01_02.html|title=Jam Trade for JamesOn Curry|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-03-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910204915/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jam_trade_for_jameson_curry_2014_01_02.html|archive-date=2016-09-10|url-status=dead}} On March 19, 2014, he was waived by the Jam due to a season-ending injury.{{Cite web |date=2015-03-28 |title=NBA Development League: Jake O'Brien Added to Jam Roster |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jake_obrien_added__jam_rost_2014_03_22.html |access-date=2023-03-04 |archive-date=2015-03-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328103619/https://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jake_obrien_added__jam_rost_2014_03_22.html |url-status=dead }} ==Legal issues== In February 2004, Curry was among 49 students arrested in a drug raid that involved [[North Carolina]]'s [[Alamance County, North Carolina|Alamance County]] school system. He was charged with two counts of possession with intent to sell and deliver [[marijuana]], two counts of sale and delivery of marijuana, and two counts of sale, possession, and delivery of a [[controlled substance]] on school grounds.{{cite news | title = Cowboys' Curry Makes Most of Second Chance | url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A35202-2005Mar14.html | date = March 15, 2005 | access-date = 2007-07-09 | last = Evans | first = Thayer | newspaper = [[The Washington Post]] }} Curry pleaded guilty to the drug charges, and the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]], with whom he had signed a letter-of-intent, rescinded the scholarship to him. In the early morning of January 17, 2008, he was arrested in [[Boise, Idaho]] and pleaded guilty to [[resisting arrest]] and urinating in public.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3201750|title=Bulls rookie Curry arrested for urinating in public|date=January 17, 2008|website=ESPN.com}} Police took him to the [[Ada County, Idaho|Ada County]] jail. He was released a few hours later after posting $600 bond. The Chicago Bulls suspended him one game after he pleaded guilty to the two misdemeanors. On October 20, 2014, Curry was arrested for marijuana possession and false representation to an officer in Edmond, Oklahoma.{{cite web | last=Schlachtenhaufen | first=Mark | title=Tail light issue leads to NBA player’s arrest | website=Norman Transcript | date=2014-10-24 | url=https://www.normantranscript.com/edmond/tail-light-issue-leads-to-nba-player-s-arrest/article_67405706-a8ff-5794-b5a1-453f5d32d36d.html | access-date=2025-06-05}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== Source:{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/curryja01.html|title=JamesOn Curry|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=10 February 2023}} ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"|{{nbay|2009}} | style="text-align:left;"|[[2009–10 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A. Clippers]] | 1 || 0 || .1 || – || – || – || .0 || .0 || .0 || .0 || .0 {{s-end}} ==Personal life== Curry was brought up on a [[tobacco]] farm in rural [[North Carolina]] in [[Pleasant Grove, North Carolina|Pleasant Grove]].{{cite news |last=Theodore |first=Conrad |title=Game on for Jameson |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_feature_071113.html |access-date=August 29, 2019 |work=NBA.com |date=November 13, 2007}} The unusual capitalization of his first name is a mix of Leon and James, honoring his father and great-uncle, respectively.{{cite news |last=Young |first=Royce |date=August 28, 2019 |title=Gone in 3.9 seconds: Where basketball took Jameson Curry |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27433858 |access-date=August 29, 2019 |work=ESPN.com}} Following the end of his basketball career, Curry moved back to his hometown, Pleasant Grove, in 2016. In April 2017, Curry was injured in a traffic collision, flipped on a freeway while trying to retrieve his dropped mobile phone. It ended his basketball career as he dislocated his ribs and fractured his lower back that needed metal rods inserted there to stabilize it.{{Citation|title=HEARTBREAKING Journey from SHORTEST NBA career to TRUCK-DRIVER|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gDDgS4YmTxw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/gDDgS4YmTxw |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|language=en|access-date=2021-10-15}}{{cbignore}} That July, he returned to Oklahoma. Subsequently, Curry worked several jobs, including as a trucker. His supervisor there asked Curry to coach the [[YMCA]] basketball team. Soon after Curry's first coaching experience, he began leading a basketball camp at Drummond High School in [[Drummond, Oklahoma]]. ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *{{basketballstats|nba=201191}} *[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3198/jameson-curry JamesOn Curry at ESPN.com] *[http://www.sportsline.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/524872 JamesOn Curry at CBS SportsLine.com] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070804000124/http://www.sportsline.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/524872 |date=2007-08-04 }} *[http://www.okstate.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=1466&SPID=145&DB_OEM_ID=200&ATCLID=73899&Q_SEASON=2005 JamesOn Curry at Oklahoma State.com]{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20060327042839/http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/jameson_curry_bio.html JamesOn Curry at USA Basketball.com] *[https://www.sbnation.com/2019/12/30/21035159/the-10-least-consequential-athletes-of-the-decade "The 10 Least Consequential Athletes of the Decade"] by [[Jon Bois]], for [[SB Nation]] {{2007 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Curry, Jameson}} [[Category:1986 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in France]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Venezuela]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Bakersfield Jam players]] [[Category:Basketball players from North Carolina]] [[Category:Chicago Bulls draft picks]] [[Category:Élan Béarnais players]] [[Category:Iowa Energy players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Clippers players]] [[Category:Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball players]] [[Category:People from Mebane, North Carolina]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Alamance County, North Carolina]] [[Category:Springfield Armor players]] [[Category:Toros de Aragua players]]
